acceptance_criteria: A tampines library module exposes the v3 loop with no GUI dependency; cargo check --target aarch64-linux-android --all-targets is clean for the tampines library.
description:
Stand up the v3 simulator as a LIBRARY in crates/tampines. No GUI, no eframe, no egui in this crate.

The boundary is already enforced by convention elsewhere: crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine documents that it carries NO physics, and src/ciet_opcua/mod.rs states it contains 'no physics and no GUI' so it compiles headless on Termux / aarch64-linux-android with no target gate. v3 must preserve that property - the tampines library must build headless for Android, and the GUI binary stays in the twin crate.

tampines already depends on outram-park-fork-coolprop (where OPCPFluidArray lives), tuas_boussinesq_solver, tampines-steam-tables, outram-foam-basic-lib, outram-foam-multiphase, chem-eng, dwsim-libs and boon-lay - so no new workspace dependency edge is needed to start.

Blocked on the naming decision.
title: CIET v3: tampines library skeleton — module layout and the physics/GUI boundary

description: The finite-difference block Jacobian does not robustly converge the buoyancy-coupled mass+energy system at the high permeability (k~1.4e-9) that supercritical Rayleigh numbers need (residual stalls ~4e-2). Add an analytic block Jacobian and/or adaptive timestepping so the two #[ignore]d HRL onset tests (buoyancy_onset_across_critical_rayleigh, heated_from_above_stays_stable) in src/thermal_convection pass. Split from op-v6s.15.6.
title: Robust convecting-regime solve for thermal_convection (HRL onset)

description: src/components/valve.rs is 49 lines: one flat rect whose green fraction tracks opening_percent. Next most valuable untabbed widget. tampines::components::Valve holds kv_max, opening_characteristic (linear / equal-percentage / quick-opening, IEC 60534) and opening_percent, and current_kv() WORKS -- so unlike the condenser and heat exchanger, a valve widget can be fully physics-driven with nothing left neutral. Draw a real body with plug lift tracking the opening, a Kv-vs-lift curve strip showing the characteristic, and a ValveKind enum (globe / gate / butterfly). mass_flow() is NotYetImplemented, so no flow rate may be drawn. Remaining untabbed after that: instrumentation (blocked -- nee_soon has no readout type), temperature_button (helper fns, not a Widget), reactor_vessel (flat rect over nee_soon NordheimFuchsExactTimestepper).
title: valve widget: real control-valve artwork + studio tab

description:
Remaining scope from op-dt3.26, which covered (p,s), the two-phase (T,p,x) family, alpha_v/kappa_t on both (T,p) and (p,h), and the TampinesSteamTableCV constructors, but deliberately left (h,s) uncovered rather than half-gate it.

STILL UNCOVERED, all panic-only:
  hs_flash_eqm::t_hs_eqm, p_hs_eqm, v_hs_eqm, x_hs_eqm, cp_hs_eqm, w_hs_eqm,
  kappa_hs_eqm, mu_hs_eqm, lambda_hs_eqm, tpvx_hs_flash_eqm, hs_flash_region,
  find_pressure_from_hs_region_4
  plus TampinesSteamTableCV::new_from_hs, which resolves pressure via p_hs_eqm
  and so inherits the whole surface.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN op-dt3.26. Unlike (p,h) and (p,s), the (h,s) panic surface is not two bound checks. Traced 2026-08-11, there are 26 distinct panic!/todo!/unimplemented! sites:

  - hs_flash_eqm/mod.rs:389,392 - global entropy band [-0.00858, 11.92] kJ/(kg K)
  - nine entropy-band sub-routers (hs_region_low_entropy_region_1_and_4 through
    hs_region_high_entropy_region_2a_only), lines 511,516,538,542,584,588,611,615,
    636,640,679,683,756,760,794,804,816,843,847,884,889,921,926 - each panics on an
    enthalpy bound computed by h_ps_eqm(p_hi, s) / h_ps_eqm(p_lo, s), i.e. by a
    (p,s) flash that itself panics
  - additional_temperature_check_for_1073_15_k_isotherm at 958,961,971,980 - two
    entropy bounds plus a resolved-temperature check that runs p_hs_2a/2b then
    t_ph_eqm (so it also inherits the (p,h) panic surface)
  - find_pressure_from_hs_region_4:1033 - 'Solution not bracketed by pressure
    bounds', a BISECTION FAILURE, not an envelope violation
  - mod.rs:365 unimplemented!('Region 5 does not have (h,s) flashing') - believed
    unreachable, no sub-router returns Region5; needs confirming, not assuming
  - validity_range.rs:50 todo!() in hs_is_below_isobar_p_100_mpa_in_region1 -
    reachable only if that fn is called with h <= 1670.9 kJ/kg and s <= 3.778
    kJ/(kg K); currently no caller inside the crate, but it is pub

A faithful gate therefore has to MIRROR the entropy-band dispatch, not add a bounds check: pick the same band, compute the same enthalpy bounds (running check_ps_envelope first so the h_ps_eqm calls are themselves safe), mirror the 1073.15 K isotherm check (with check_ph_envelope before its t_ph_eqm), and then gate the post-routing calls too, since tpvx_hs_flash_eqm goes on to call v_ps_eqm(p_resolved, s) and x_ph_flash(p_resolved, h) with a pressure that comes out of a backward equation.

The bisection panic at :1033 cannot be gated by any input bounds check. Recommend find_pressure_from_hs_region_4 be changed to return Result (a separate, non-additive change needing maintainer sign-off), or the checked (h,s) facade be documented as covering the envelope panics only - which by the op-dt3.26 no-half-gating rule means it should not ship until that is resolved.

REQUIRED PATTERN (unchanged from op-t647/op-dt3.26): no catch_unwind ever; NaN rejected explicitly; typed errors; uom on the public surface; doc comments stating physical quantity, valid range and units; a panic-site-to-gate table in the module doc; and a sweep of the accepted set proving zero leaked panics before the gate is called complete.
title: tampines-steam-tables: bounds-checked facade for the (h,s) flash family

description: O(n^3) -> O(n) in the hottest loop of the only fidelity band that currently runs in real time. thomas_solve already exists in the crate. Pair with the criterion harness bead so the improvement is measured, not asserted.
title: tuas: replace the dense LU on the tridiagonal conductance matrix with thomas_solve

description:

  app::tests::the_gui_defaults_are_the_plant_command_defaults
  physics::secondary_loop::tests::feedwater_flow_tracks_duty_and_stays_in_range
  physics::secondary_loop::tests::manual_feedwater_holds_the_commanded_flow_and_auto_does_not
  physics::secondary_loop::tests::manual_rebuilds_the_controller
  physics::secondary_loop::tests::the_gui_ranges_match_the_physics_clamps
  physics::turbine_generator::tests::the_plant_settles_the_shaft_a_little_under_synchronous_speed

VERIFIED PRE-EXISTING AND UNRELATED: git stash'd every change made for op-mmep (Cargo.toml example registration, components/mod.rs's new distillation_column module) and re-ran cargo test --release -p outram-park-digital-twin-engine --example htgr_sim_v1 -- the_gui_defaults_are_the_plant_command_defaults on the bare develop tree (commit 9229031d62) -- same failure, same panic message ('the GUI must open in AUTO' at app/mod.rs:765). notes.content:
ADDITIONAL PRE-EXISTING GAP found in the same sweep, also unrelated to op-mmep, also verified via git-stash on bare develop (9229031d62): fhr_sim_v2 and widget_studio both FAIL to Android-check under cargo check -p outram-park-digital-twin-engine --lib --example <name> --target aarch64-linux-android:
  - fhr_sim_v2: E0433 'could not find app in the crate root' -- main.rs references crate::app::... unconditionally even though pub mod app; is #[cfg(not(target_os = "android"))]-gated (main.rs:33 vs :421-422). The android stub main() this crate's convention requires (see htgr_sim_v1/main.rs and the new distillation_sim_v1/main.rs) is missing or incomplete.
  - widget_studio: 197 errors, unresolved crate egui -- egui is itself target-gated off Android in Cargo.toml, and widget_studio has no Android stub main gating its egui-using modules out, unlike htgr_sim_v1/distillation_sim_v1.

CONTRAST: htgr_sim_v1 and the new distillation_sim_v1 (op-mmep) both Android-check CLEAN (cargo check -p outram-park-digital-twin-engine --lib --example distillation_sim_v1 --example htgr_sim_v1 --target aarch64-linux-android succeeds) -- both follow the '#[cfg(target_os = "android")] fn main() {}' stub + gated mod app/mod physics pattern documented in this crate's CLAUDE.md. fhr_sim_v2 and widget_studio predate or don't follow that convention.

So the crate's own mandatory rule ('cargo check -p outram-park-digital-twin-engine --target aarch64-linux-android' Android check) currently only passes when run --lib-only or scoped to the two conforming examples; a full --all-targets run fails on the two non-conforming ones. Not investigated further or fixed -- out of scope for op-mmep.

title: digital-twin-engine: 6 pre-existing htgr_sim_v1 test failures, unrelated to distillation_sim_v1

description:
Replace three near-duplicate bounded time-history implementations with one generic type
in app_scaffold: HtgrPlotData (examples/htgr_sim_v1/app/state.rs, Vec + remove(0), O(n)
shift per sample) and the CIET-v1-derived PagePlotData lineage shared by
ciet_educational_simulator_v2 (ciet_simulator_v2/app/panels_and_pages/ciet_data.rs) and
fhr_sim_v2 (examples/fhr_sim_v2/app/graph_data/mod.rs) -- both insert-at-front then
rebuild a fixed NUM_DATA_PTS_IN_PLOTS=4000-element Vec on every single sample.

Design: PlotHistory<T, const N: usize> on VecDeque<T>, push() O(1) amortized, oldest-first
iterator (egui_plot-friendly, matches HTGR's existing convention). Plain generic, no
trait objects, fits Arc<RwLock<T>> / SharedState<PlotHistory<T,N>> for the existing
sampler-thread pattern.

This is additive -- no existing call site is migrated onto it in this pass (that would
touch htgr_sim_v1/app/state.rs, which is off-limits to this session per a concurrent
fast-forward-control edit, and would touch ciet_educational_simulator_v2/fhr_sim_v2,
which the workspace CLAUDE.md biases against doing as a risky same-pass migration).
Migrating existing call sites onto it is separate follow-up work once this lands.

Surveyed 2026-08-17, read-only, by a fork agent; report retained in op-wqk.22.
title: app_scaffold: generic PlotHistory<T,N> ring buffer for plot panels

description:
Foundation for the rest of `op-yvj.4`. Everything else depends on this.

Deliver the dispatch layer itself, no kernels:

- `ComputeBackend { Serial, CpuMulti, Gpu }` — enum dispatch, per the workspace
  Rust design rules (no `dyn`, no `Box`, no lifetime params). Shared GPU device
  / queue state held as `Arc<T>`.
- A **backend-selection policy** that is explicit and documented: what problem
  size or batch count makes a GPU dispatch worth the host-device transfer, and
  what happens below it (fall back to `CpuMulti`, then `Serial`). Auto-select
  must be a named function a reader can find, not scattered `if n > 1024`.
- **Cargo features**: `gpu` (wgpu) and `parallel` (rayon), both **off by
  default** so the default build stays Android-clean and dependency-light.
- **Android/Termux gating** (hard rule, epic `op-zfr`): wgpu declared only
  under `[target.'cfg(not(target_os = "android"))'.dependencies]`; every
  GPU-touching test/bench carries `#![cfg(not(target_os = "android"))]` and
  every GPU-touching example gets an Android stub `main`. Acceptance is
  `cargo check -p outram-foam-basic-lib --all-targets --target
  aarch64-linux-android` clean, with a native Termux build as the
  authoritative check.
- **Graceful absence of a GPU**: no adapter, no panic — log once and fall back.
- Module-level `//!` doc explaining what belongs in the backend module and what
  does not (human-interface-layer rule).

Look at how `njoy-outram-park-fork` and `outram-mc-libs` (`op-u6s.3`) already
gate their wgpu paths and reuse that shape rather than inventing a third one.
If the shape generalises, note whether it should eventually live in one place
instead of three.
title: outram-foam-basic-lib: ComputeBackend enum (Serial/CpuMulti/Gpu) + dispatch policy + feature/Android gating
